editorial:
Imagine being stuck in a place where every choice you make could get you or someone else killed. You follow Jorge Silva, an Air Force captain in Chile during the 1973 military coup. The movie puts you right inside a military base where the mood is tense and scary from the start. You get to see Jorge struggle as he realizes the people he works for are doing terrible things to innocent prisoners. It feels like a race against time as he tries to keep his own soul intact while surrounded by people who have lost theirs. 

The acting is top-notch and makes you feel Jorge's fear and guilt in every scene. While the story starts a bit slow, it picks up speed and keeps you on the edge of your seat. If you like stories about brave people doing the right thing when it is hard, you will love this. You should definitely stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video to see all the gritty details, or maybe rent it on Apple TV for a quick movie night. If you are a movie collector, adding the 4K Blu-ray to your shelf is a great call.
endingExplained: At the end, Jorge decides he cannot stay silent anymore. He risks his life to sneak prisoners out of the hangar and help them escape. In a final twist, he is caught by his own superiors, but he manages to save a few lives before being arrested. The movie wraps up with a sad but hopeful look at how his small act of kindness mattered in a time of great hate.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves historical dramas and stories about moral courage.
